page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance built on the arm64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores using AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors clocked at 2.6 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 128 GB of DDR5 RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and provides a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Hardware accelerators like GPUs are not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute efficiency alongside high memory and network throughput. The instance ranks in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core performance (20,886.0) and Clang software compilation (59,675.0), supported by top-tier PassMark memory performance. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 98,074.28, and Redis set operations hit 101.71 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain moderate, with single-core Geekbench scoring 1,549.0 and single-core stress-ng reaching 1,535.78. LLM text generation throughput is restricted, scoring in the bottom tier on smaller models due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration hardware.

Without hyperthreading contention or hypervisor overhead, c7gn.metal maximizes per-core consistency and network throughput. It is technically suitable for distributed data processing, continuous integration build pipelines, network-intensive appliances, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-bandwidth-dependent computational jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server featuring 64 dedicated arm64 physical cores powered by AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors operating at 2.6 GHz. Operating without hyperthreading or virtualization layers, the server provides direct hardware execution backed by 128 GB of DDR5 memory and 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage and lacks discrete GPUs. Multi-core performance is strong, registering top-tier results in software compilation and PassMark memory benchmarks, complemented by over 101 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Single-thread performance is moderate across standard benchmarks, and language model text generation is constrained by the absence of specialized tensor hardware. With its high networking ceiling and clean physical core layout, c7gn.metal is well tailored for intensive compilation pipelines, network packet processing, container clusters, and distributed memory-bound applications.
